subject: Route220 (IT*220) first-party direct-tariff investigation after Atlante/IONITY integrations

decision.reason: Current first-party Route220 surfaces confirm CPMS-managed networks can use independently configured tariffs and integrated POS/app payment, but no current deterministic IT*220 network-wide or class-wide direct price was found. A generic Route220/evway price must therefore not be transposed to the IT*220 canonical perimeter.
decision.blockingCondition: Obtain a deterministic station/EVSE -> direct CPO price surface (QR/POS/guest/backend) for IT*220, or an official current rule proving a network/class-wide tariff for the exact IT*220 perimeter.
decision.confidence: high that no network-wide tariff can be inferred from the inspected first-party material; unresolved station-level tariff mapping remains fail-closed

positiveEvidence.finding: Route220 states its CPMS lets independent CPOs manage their own network and tariffs, with payment through POS or customized app; this proves tariff configurability rather than a single Route220-wide price.
Route220 documents evwaypay as registration-free POS payment infrastructure for CPOs, but the page publishes no deterministic IT*220 station price.
Route220 identifies evway as its driver charging app and Route220 as CPMS/consulting provider; this is insufficient to equate evway roaming prices with CPO-direct IT*220 tariffs.

negativePaths: Current Route220 tariff/site searches did not expose an official network-wide IT*220 EUR/kWh grid.
evway/eMSP pricing is not accepted as Route220 CPO-direct pricing without exact channel equivalence.
CPMS tariff-management capability is not evidence that all IT*220 stations share one tariff.

antiStagnation.nextAction: Move to the next large station-level partial or reconcile unreconciled PUN partyIds; do not repeat generic Route220 tariff search without a concrete QR/EVSE/backend lead.
